clue.text: Tenerife can't supply a place for surfing

indicators.note: read as the adverb of 'supple', supply means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble that the Canary Island resort cannot offer anywhere to go surfing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb from supple, bending the letters of TENERIFE CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfing here is browsing the web, and a café offering computers with online access is a spot to do that.

clue.text: Sloth, one in a tree, almost moving

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: letters on the move are being rearranged into a new order
almost the whole word, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A sloth, the animal, hanging in a tree and barely moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The sloth seems to be the animal in the tree, but it is the deadly sin; 'almost' cuts the last letter before 'moving' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth as the vice of laziness is synonymous with inertia, a reluctance to act or change.

clue.text: Coach from Timbuktu to Rabat

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A coach journey across West Africa, from Mali's Timbuktu to the Moroccan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to teach them privately, which is what a tutor does.

clue.text: Raise children with guardians in a retrograde way

parts.note: to rear children is to raise them
wards are minors placed under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A complaint that bringing up children alongside guardians is old-fashioned parenting.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrograde means moving backwards, so acting in a retrograde way is going backwards or towards the rear.

clue.text: A head teacher's part

indicators.note: only a part of the word is used, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of a head teacher's role in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head teacher' reads as one phrase, but 'A head' is the definition and the answer sits within 'teacher's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices quoted 'a head' are per person, the same sense as so much for every one.

clue.text: Rotter, very anxious, carrying clubs in a bag

parts.note: a cad is an old word for a dishonourable man, a rotter
dying to do something is being very eager or anxious to

explanation.surface: A nervous scoundrel lugging golf clubs around in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's bag of clubs around the course, so that work is the activity described.

clue.text: Lacking strength, don't pass around river

indicators.note: the first piece sits around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: to fail an exam is not to pass it
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A weak swimmer is told not to go around a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frail is weak and delicate, physically lacking in robustness.

clue.text: As well as tucking into Guinness, maybe distinguish oneself

indicators.note: one piece is tucked inside the other, held within it

parts.note: Guinness is an example of stout, a dark beer
and means as well as

explanation.surface: Someone tucking into a pint of Guinness hoping to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like enjoying a drink, but it is the container signal; Guinness is the famous Irish stout.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out is to be conspicuous or excel, making oneself noticeable among others.

clue.text: Morally pure Conservative rushing around?

parts.note: haste is hurry, rushing about

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a virtuous Tory politician is always dashing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste describes someone virtuous and abstaining from sex, hence pure in morals.

clue.text: Held spellbound in door number four?

parts.note: an entrance is a door or way in
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet, as gates or doors are lettered

explanation.surface: Someone captivated while standing in a doorway marked number four.
explanation.walkthrough: Doors at a venue are often lettered, so 'door number four' becomes entrance D.
explanation.definitionFit: Entranced means captivated or enthralled, as if under a magic spell.

clue.text: A long letter dropped in East London

definitions.text: A long letter dropped in East London

parts.words: A long letter dropped in East London
parts.note: the letter H written out in full is a long-looking word, and Cockney speech famously drops that sound

explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, the traditional working-class Londoners of the East End, leave the H off words like 'ouse; the letter's name spelt out makes it 'long'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet is the word the clue describes.

clue.text: Confused personnel entering urban area

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, inside it

parts.note: a town is an urban area
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Bewildered staff arriving in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown, as in 'thrown by the question', means disconcerted or bewildered.

clue.text: Bikes going round Oregon's borders in strong winds

indicators.note: the first piece wraps round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: cycles are bikes

indicators.note: the borders of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the state name, taken as written

explanation.surface: Cyclists battling gales on a tour around the edges of the US state of Oregon.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclones are violent rotating storms with very high winds.

clue.text: Insist Parisian's very charming quality comes back

indicators.note: coming back means the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: très is French for very
SA, sex appeal, is an attractive, charming quality

explanation.surface: A Parisian insisting their great charm is returning.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state forcefully, to insist that something is so.

clue.text: Shocking event stirred up Spurs' ire

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A shock result that riled Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club nicknamed Spurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise is an unexpected occurrence that startles, a shock.

clue.text: Sun running British reporter's experiences in short feature

indicators.note: letters that are running are in motion, reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what a reporter speaks is heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: to know hardship is to experience it, so knows means experiences

explanation.surface: A Sun journalist's encounters, written up in a brief newspaper feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun', the British tabloid, is anagram fodder; KNOWS spoken aloud is NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, turned-up nose is a facial feature, so the definition is literal rather than journalistic.

clue.text: Loudly deride dessert getting stick in Australia

indicators.note: spoken loudly, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to boo is to deride, and meringue is a dessert, giving boo meringue

explanation.surface: Jeering at a pudding before eating in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loudly' seems to describe the jeering but asks you to say BOO MERINGUE aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The boomerang is a curved throwing stick traditionally used by Aboriginal Australians.

clue.text: Ms Toksvig and I in Californian city

parts.note: Sandi Toksvig is a Danish-born British broadcaster, host of QI
the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: A traveller visiting a Californian city with Sandi Toksvig.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large coastal city in southern California.

clue.text: 1,000 boats by British isle for a 28 Across?

definitions.note: the cross-reference is the shooting star, read playfully as one who is a star at shooting

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
arks are boats, as Noah's was
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A thousand boats moored by the Isle of Man for a big name.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 Across is SHOOTING STAR, read here as someone brilliant at shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is an expert shot, so playfully a star of shooting.

clue.text: One brings luck, heading for motor racing venue

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English horse racecourse

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a lucky charm sets off by car for the races.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object believed to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Scrape pan from Asia, turning to wife

indicators.note: turning the word round runs its letters the other way

parts.note: a wok is an Asian cooking pan

explanation.surface: Scrubbing an Asian pan before turning to one's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrape' is a verb as in 'bow and scrape', not cleaning a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape, in the idiom bow and scrape, is to grovel obsequiously, exactly as kowtowing is.

clue.text: Empty talk mostly painful for royal family

parts.note: wind is empty, pointless talk

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: Idle gossip that is hurtful to the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor is the house name of the current British royal dynasty.

clue.text: Very calm about publicity for love song

indicators.note: the first piece goes about the second, around it

parts.note: serene means very calm
an ad, advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A singer cool about the promotion of their ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song sung beneath a lover's window, a romantic piece of music.

clue.text: Weight lifted by children or Mark

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word up makes it read bottom to top

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A weightlifting contest open to children or to someone called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small cut or mark, as on a stick or belt.

clue.text: Ex-president of America beset by terrible anger

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so one piece is enclosed in the other
terrible signals the letters being badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A former US president besieged by furious rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns ANGER into REGAN, and that wraps the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the 40th president of the United States, serving 1981 to 1989.

clue.text: Invitee speculated on the radio

indicators.note: a radio broadcast is heard, so the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: guessed means speculated

explanation.surface: A guest who was asked to speculate during a radio interview.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a person who has been invited to a party, show or home.

clue.text: You heard American soldier eating large fruit

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: the letter U is said like the word you

indicators.note: the eater holds the eaten inside it

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a US soldier is eating a big piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo with wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Start working with TV or radio, say

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a TV or radio is a set, a receiving device

explanation.surface: Beginning a job in broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, its start.

clue.text: English people at discos — they make an impression

parts.note: ravers are people who go to raves and dance parties

explanation.surface: English clubbers who make an impact on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make an impression' sounds figurative, but engravers literally cut impressions into metal or wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Engravers cut designs into plates, which are then used to print impressions.

clue.text: Sky viewer may see this celebrity after making film

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a meteor streaking across the night sky
second meaning: a star who is shooting, i.e. filming, a movie

explanation.surface: A stargazer and a famous actor on location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' suggests the British satellite TV channel; it is the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is popularly called by this name, and a film star is shooting while making a picture.
